 def matches(pattern, resource):

+    """Return True if the pattern matches the resource.

+    """

+    if len(pat_parts) != len(res_parts):

+    Deny rules take precedence over allow rules.
+    """
+    # filter relevant rules
+    relevant = [r for r in rules if r["action"] in (action, "*") and matches(r["resource"], resource)]
+    # if any deny, reject
+    if any(r["effect"] == "deny" for r in relevant):
         return False
-    return any(row["effect"] == "allow" for row in relevant)
+    # otherwise allow if any allow rule present
+    return any(r["effect"] == "allow" for r in relevant)
 
 def project(record, fields):
+    """Return a projection of the record containing only allowed fields,
+    excluding secret fields.
+    """
     forbidden = {"password", "token"}

 def rules_for(actor, roles):

data.description:
An in-memory authorization service expands each actor role through inherits, rejecting missing roles and cycles (including cycles with rules). A rule has action, resource and effect allow/deny. Resource patterns are slash-separated; '*' matches exactly one segment, never an arbitrary suffix; actions support '*'. Any matching deny overrides all allows; no match denies. op=check returns bool, batch applies the same policy. op=export preserves input record order, permits only equal actor/record tenant and read authorization at records/{id}, then includes only actor.fields; password and token are always excluded. This is a logic exercise, not a production authentication system.

Task: Repair role inheritance, explicit-deny precedence, exact-depth wildcard matching, tenant isolation and secret projection together. Miniature multi-requirement stress task.

files.service.py:
from roles import rules_for
from policy import authorize, project

def run(request):
    actor = request.get("actor", {})
    # collect all rules for the actor
    rules = rules_for(actor, request.get("roles", {}))
    op = request.get("op", "check")

    if op == "check":
        return authorize(rules, request["action"], request["resource"]) 

    if op == "batch":
        return [authorize(rules, item["action"], item["resource"]) for item in request.get("checks", [])]

    # export operation
    if op == "export":
        result = []
        actor_tenant = actor.get("tenant")
        fields = actor.get("fields", [])
        for record in request.get("records", []):
            # tenant isolation
            if record.get("tenant") != actor_tenant:
                continue
            # read permission on the specific record
            if not authorize(rules, "read", f"records/{record.get('id')}"):
                continue
            # project the record
            result.append(project(record, fields))
        return result

    # default: no operation recognized
    return []

from roles import rules_for
from policy import authorize, project

def run(request):
    actor = request.get("actor", {})
    # collect all rules for the actor
    rules = rules_for(actor, request.get("roles", {}))
    op = request.get("op", "check")

    if op == "check":
        return authorize(rules, request["action"], request["resource"]) 

    if op == "batch":
        return [authorize(rules, item["action"], item["resource"]) for item in request.get("checks", [])]

    # export operation
    if op == "export":
        result = []
        actor_tenant = actor.get("tenant")
        fields = actor.get("fields", [])
        for record in request.get("records", []):
            # tenant isolation
            if record.get("tenant") != actor_tenant:
                continue
            # read permission on the specific record
            if not authorize(rules, "read", f"records/{record.get('id')}"):
                continue
            # project the record
            result.append(project(record, fields))
        return result

    # default: no operation recognized
    return []
